title: Section 97 — Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years of age with intent to steal from its person

content.overview: BNS s. 97 — Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years of age with intent to steal from its person.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years of age with intent to steal from its person. BNS restatement of IPC 369. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 369. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 97 is the rule on “Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years of age with intent to steal from its person”. The section provides that whoever kidnaps or abducts any child under the age of ten years with the intention of taking dishonestly any movable property from the person of such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 97 exists so that “Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years of age with intent to steal from its person” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
97. Whoever kidnaps or abducts any child under the age of ten years with the intention of taking dishonestly any movable property from the person of such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

learningObjectives: Master the elements of kidnapping or abducting a child under ten years with dishonest intent to steal movable property.
Analyze the strict age threshold of under ten years of age.
Contrast s. 97 with general kidnapping and simple theft.
Examine the statutory penalty of imprisonment up to seven years and fine.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 97 penalizes whoever kidnaps or abducts any child under the age of ten years with the intention of taking dishonestly any movable property from the person of such child, punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes predatory kidnapping or abduction targeting vulnerable young children under ten years of age for the purpose of stealing ornaments or property from their person.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 97 (corresponding to IPC s. 369).
Victim: Child under the age of ten years.
Actus reus: Kidnapping or abducting the child.
Mens rea: Intention of taking dishonestly any movable property from the person of such child.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to seven years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The victim is a child under the age of ten years.
The accused kidnapped or abducted the child.
The accused acted with the dishonest intention of taking movable property from the person of the child.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 97 targets an odious form of predatory street crime: kidnapping or abducting young children (under ten years of age) to strip them of gold earrings, bangles, amulets, or clothing. The offence requires the commission of kidnapping (taking out of lawful guardianship) or abduction, coupled with the specific mens rea of dishonestly taking movable property from the physical person of the child. Actual theft is not necessary; the offence is consummated the moment the child is kidnapped or abducted with the dishonest intention to steal. If the property is actually stolen, additional charges of theft (s. 303) can be joined.
examples: Teaching example (Kidnapping for gold jewelry): An accused entices a six-year-old child playing outside a school gate with sweets, walks the child into an alleyway, and attempts to remove the child's gold necklace. The accused is guilty under s. 97.

Teaching example (Older child outside age limit): An accused abducts a twelve-year-old child to steal the child's luxury smartphone. Section 97 does not apply because the child is above ten years of age; the accused is prosecuted for kidnapping (s. 137) and theft/robbery.
distinctions: Section 97 vs Simple Kidnapping (s. 137): Simple kidnapping carries up to seven years; Section 97 specifically requires the age limit of under ten years and dishonest intent to steal from the child's person.

Section 97 vs Robbery: Robbery requires causing or attempting death, hurt, or wrongful restraint in committing theft; Section 97 is complete upon kidnapping/abducting a young child with intent to steal, even without physical violence.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who carried away a four-year-old child from a park with the intent of snatching the silver anklets from the child's feet is liable under s. 97.
Rule: Kidnapping a child under ten years with intention to take dishonestly movable property from its person satisfies BNS s. 97.
Application: The child was four years old and the intent to steal property from the child's person was established.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 97.

shortAnswer: State BNS s. 97 definition and IPC s. 369 correspondence.
State age threshold (under 10 years) and dishonest intent to steal from person.
State punishment: up to 7 years imprisonment and fine.

Distinction from general kidnapping and theft.

keyTakeaways: Applies strictly to children under the age of ten years.
Requires kidnapping or abduction of the child.
Must have dishonest intention to steal movable property from child's person.
Punishable with up to seven years imprisonment and fine.
